# d3

The 27B Decision 3.0 model, the family's largest, for your own questions about text, images and video. Its quantized packages hold it in a third to three fifths of the memory.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Repository | [`vllm-sr/d3`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3), pinned at `cbff3a3cb0b0` |
| Family | [Decision 3.0](model-runtime/supported-models/decision-3/overview.md) |
| Parameters | 26.1B loaded |
| Backbone | Qwen3.5 text |
| Precision (`--dtype auto`) | BF16 on a GPU, FP32 on a CPU |
| Weights | about 52.2 GB at BF16, 104.3 GB at FP32 |
| Device memory | 72 GiB or more |
| Reads | text, image, video |

## Question types

| Type | Answers |
| --- | --- |
| `choice` | Yes |
| `noul` | Yes |
| `score` | Yes |
| `set` | Yes, asked as one `noul` per label |
| `span` | No: bind span questions, such as PII and hallucination, to a span-capable model |

Rules that read the turn's images (`input.image`) or videos (`input.video`) can
resolve to it.

## Built-in questions

The Decision 3.0 family answers the Router's built-in questions
zero-shot, from their canonical wording; the
[support matrix](system-one/reference/support-matrix.md) shows what that
covers.

:::note
This model has no calibrated thresholds: a built-in question without a
`predicate` uses 0.5, and the configuration load warns with
`uncalibrated_preset`.
:::

## Hardware

Each time it loads, the model compares its answers with the reference
answers recorded for its revision. They are recorded for:

- CPU (`cpu`)
- AMD GPU (ROCm) (`rocm`)

Served with `--dtype bfloat16`, it compares them with the BF16
references recorded for:

- CPU (`cpu@bfloat16`)
- x86-64 CPU with AVX2 (BF16 emulated) (`cpu:x86_64:avx2:bf16_emulated@bfloat16`)
- x86-64 CPU with AVX-512 BF16 (`cpu:x86_64:avx512:bf16_native@bfloat16`)

Where a hardware reference and its device class's are both recorded, the
hardware one is checked.

On an NVIDIA GPU no reference is recorded, so the model serves
there with its self-check reported as `unverified`.

[Choose a model](model-runtime/get-started/choose-a-model.md#hardware) lists the
validated hardware.

## Quantization

The Decision 3.0 family loads quantized packages in the
compressed-tensors format: FP8 (W8A8), int4 (W4A16, GPTQ or AWQ) and NVFP4
(W4A4). A quantized package is its own model, with its own answers.

Published packages of this model:

- [`vllm-sr/d3-FP8`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3-FP8)
- [`vllm-sr/d3-W4A16-AWQ`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3-W4A16-AWQ)
- [`vllm-sr/d3-W4A16-GPTQ`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3-W4A16-GPTQ)
- [`vllm-sr/d3-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3-NVFP4)
- [`vllm-sr/d3-NVFP4-AWQ`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3-NVFP4-AWQ)

[Quantization](model-runtime/quantization/overview.md) compares the formats and
the hardware each needs.

## Deploy it

Serve it on its own in Engine mode, to ask it directly:

<Tabs groupId="platform">
<TabItem value="cpu" label="CPU">

```bash
vllm-sr serve vllm-sr/d3 --engine --platform cpu
```

Serve it on a CPU from the CPU image, as `--platform cpu` does: the ROCm
image's PyTorch has no CPU LAPACK, which this backbone needs there.

A CPU computes it in FP32: 104.3 GB of weights, twice its
BF16 size. On a CPU that computes BF16 natively (AVX-512 BF16 or AMX) a
request takes 1.2 to 3.5 times as long as at `--dtype bfloat16`, the larger
sizes the most; on one that emulates BF16 (AVX2) FP32 is 3 to 6 times
faster. `--dtype bfloat16` is checked against the BF16 reference of its CPU
class (see Hardware).

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="rocm" label="AMD GPU" default>

```bash
vllm-sr serve vllm-sr/d3 --engine --platform rocm
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="cuda" label="NVIDIA GPU">

```bash
vllm-sr serve vllm-sr/d3 --engine --platform cuda
```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Or make it the Router's decision model:

```yaml title="config.yaml"
global:
  model_catalog:
    deployments:
      primary:
        provider: model_runtime
        artifact: vllm-sr/d3
        device: auto
      spans:
        provider: model_runtime
        artifact: vllm-sr/vela3-fast
    bindings:
      pii: spans
      hallucination: spans
    system:
      decision_model: {deployment: primary}
```

`device: auto` takes the first validated GPU with enough free memory, else
the CPU; name `rocm:0` or `cuda:0` to pin a GPU.

This model answers no span questions, so the example keeps `pii` and
`hallucination` on a span-capable deployment; without those bindings a
`pii` rule fails to load with `span_required`.

To run it on another host and attach the Router to it:

```bash
vllm-srun serve vllm-sr/d3 --device auto --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8100
```

Then set `endpoint: http://<host>:8100` and
`model: d3` on the deployment; see
[Attach to a runtime you run](model-runtime/deploy/connect-the-router.md#attach-to-a-runtime-you-run).
